docs.title: Soundwave
docs.text:
Soundwave is an experimental acoustic modem. It sends short messages and small files between nearby devices over high-frequency sound, using an ordinary speaker and microphone. No network, Bluetooth or pairing is involved.

The project has two parts:

  • native/: a portable C11 DSP core (libsoundwave). It provides CRC-32, Reed-Solomon RS(255,223), chirp (CSS) and OFDM modems, frame sync, CFO estimation, channel estimation and equalization, AGC, and miniaudio-based audio I/O behind a C ABI (soundwave_api.h). The same directory holds the soundwave-cli developer tool.
  • soundwave_app/: a Flutter app for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux. It calls the core through dart:ffi and adds a link layer (fragmentation, file transfer, optional stop-and-wait ARQ), live spectrum, waterfall and constellation views, WAV recording, import and export, and onboarding.

Status: pre-release, no field measurements yet

All acoustic performance figures on this site are design targets, values derived from the code, or simulations (AWGN in CI). Each figure is labeled as one of these. No over-the-air measurement has been made with real devices yet; see the field test plan.

docs.title: C API Reference (soundwave_api.h)
docs.text:
This page is maintained by hand and checked against native/include/soundwave_api.h, native/include/soundwave/types.h and native/src/api/ (soundwave_api.c, ffi_helpers.c). The Doxygen reference is generated from the header comments on every docs build. Where a header comment and the implementation disagree, this page follows the implementation and says so.

  • Linkage: extern "C". Symbols are exported with SW_API (__declspec(dllexport) when building the Windows DLL, visibility("default") elsewhere).
  • Version macro: SW_VERSION "1.0.0".
  • Return convention: int status, SW_OK (0) on success, a negative sw_error_t otherwise.
  • Memory: the caller allocates all output buffers. The library never keeps or frees caller pointers. Handles returned by *_start / *_create are owned by the library and freed by the matching *_stop / *_destroy.

docs.title: Status codes (sw_error_t)
docs.text: Code Value Returned when SW_OK 0 Success SW_ERR_BAD_PARAM −1 NULL pointer, zero length/capacity, or a config rejected by sw_config_validate SW_ERR_MEMORY −2 Allocation failed SW_ERR_DECODE −3 Reed-Solomon decode failed (more than t errors) SW_ERR_SYNC −4 No preamble found, or too few samples for sync/CFO SW_ERR_AUDIO −5 Audio device error SW_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED −6 Feature not implemented SW_ERR_OVERFLOW −7 Output buffer too small. The length out-parameter then holds the required size

docs.title: Configuration (sw_config_t)
docs.text:
typedef struct {
    int   sample_rate;      // Hz; 0 = 44100
    int   modulation;       // 0 = CSS, 1 = OFDM
    int   sf;               // CSS spreading factor 6..10 (0 = 8): SF bits per chirp
    int   num_subcarriers;  // OFDM FFT size N (power of two, 16..4096; 0 = 256)
    int   cp_length;        // OFDM cyclic prefix in samples (0..N; 0 = N/8)
    int   num_pilots;       // OFDM pilots (0..N/2; see note)
    float coding_rate;      // reserved, ignored (must be finite); FEC is fixed RS(255,223)
    float threshold;        // detection threshold multiplier (>= 0)
    int   equalizer;        // 0 = ZF, 1 = MMSE
    float carrier_freq;     // Hz; CSS band centre fc, OFDM band centre (0 = 19000)
    float bandwidth;        // Hz; CSS sweep (used as fs / round(fs / bandwidth)), OFDM band width (0 = 2000)
    float symbol_duration;  // s; ignored by CSS (T = 2^sf / B); validated <= 1.0
    float amplitude;        // transmit peak, (0, 1] (0 = 0.8): max |sample| <= amplitude
    int   ofdm_modulation;  // 0 = BPSK, 1 = QPSK
} sw_config_t;

Field notes (from the implementation):

  • Zero means default for most fields. Each module fills in its own default.
  • sf sets the CSS symbol: one chirp of \(2^{SF}\) chips carries SF bits (cyclically shifted up-chirps, Gray mapped). The chirp lasts \(2^{SF}/B\), so symbol_duration is not used by CSS.
  • coding_rate is reserved and ignored: the only FEC is the fixed RS(255,223) code applied by the caller (app/CLI). num_pilots is validated but does not change the waveform: OFDM puts a pilot on every 8th active subcarrier regardless of num_pilots.
  • amplitude is the transmit peak level. Every frame from sw_css_modulate and sw_ofdm_modulate satisfies max |sample| ≤ amplitude ≤ 1, so it can be played or written as 16-bit PCM without clipping (clipping would splatter energy into the audible band). CSS chirps have a constant envelope of exactly amplitude. OFDM frames are multiplied by one gain per frame so that their peak equals amplitude (deterministic peak normalization); the RMS level is therefore lower by the frame's crest factor and varies slightly from frame to frame. A single gain is a flat channel to the receiver (preamble channel estimate, AGC), so demodulation is unaffected.
  • carrier_freq and bandwidth also set the OFDM band \([f_c - B/2, f_c + B/2]\) (default 18–20 kHz). Only subcarriers inside it (with one guard bin per edge) carry data or pilots. sw_config_validate (for modulation == 1) and every sw_ofdm_* function reject a band that reaches DC, lies within one subcarrier spacing of Nyquist, or holds fewer than 4 subcarriers (see Signal chain).

docs.title: sw_config_validate
docs.text:
int sw_config_validate(sw_config_t cfg);

Returns SW_OK or SW_ERR_BAD_PARAM. Every sw_* function that takes a config calls it first. It checks:

  • modulation, equalizer and ofdm_modulation are each 0 or 1.
  • sample_rate is 0 or in 8000..192000.
  • All float fields are finite.
  • threshold, carrier_freq, bandwidth and symbol_duration are ≥ 0.
  • carrier_freq and bandwidth are ≤ Nyquist.
  • symbol_duration ≤ 1 s.
  • amplitude is in [0, 1] (0 selects 0.8).
  • sf is 0 or 6..10.
  • CSS (modulation 0) only: the band carrier_freq ± B/2 lies in (0, Nyquist] and a symbol \(2^{SF}/B\) is at most 1 s, with B = fs / round(fs / bandwidth).
  • num_subcarriers is 0 or a power of two in 16..4096.
  • cp_length is in 0..N.
  • num_pilots is in 0..N/2.
  • OFDM (modulation 1) only: the band carrier_freq ± bandwidth/2 lies above DC, its upper edge is at most fs/2 − fs/N, and it holds at least 4 subcarriers after one guard bin per edge. The sw_ofdm_* functions apply this check whatever modulation says.

docs.title: CRC-32
docs.text:
int sw_crc32(const uint8_t* data, size_t len, uint32_t* crc);

IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 (reflected, polynomial 0xEDB88320). len == 0 yields *crc = 0. Returns SW_ERR_BAD_PARAM for NULL data or crc.

docs.title: Reed-Solomon RS(255,223)
docs.text:
int sw_rs_encode(const uint8_t* data, size_t data_len,
                 uint8_t* parity, size_t* parity_len);
int sw_rs_decode(uint8_t* data, size_t* data_len,
                 const uint8_t* parity, size_t parity_len,
                 int* errors_corrected);
  • sw_rs_encode: data_len must be 1..223. It writes 32 parity bytes and sets *parity_len = 32. Shorter messages are treated as a shortened code.
  • sw_rs_decode: corrects up to 16 byte errors in place in data (the parity is read-only). Constraints: *data_len in 1..255, parity_len ≥ 2, and *data_len + parity_len ≤ 255. Returns SW_ERR_DECODE when the word is uncorrectable. On success *errors_corrected is 0..16.

docs.title: CSS modem
docs.text:
int sw_css_modulate(const uint8_t* bits, size_t bit_len, sw_config_t cfg,
                    float* samples, size_t* sample_len);
int sw_css_demodulate(const float* samples, size_t sample_len, sw_config_t cfg,
                      uint8_t* bits, size_t* bit_len);
  • Bit packing: bits is a packed byte array (MSB first). bit_len counts bits.
  • Output length: sw_css_modulate produces (10 + ceil(bit_len / SF)) × 2^SF × D samples, D = round(fs / bandwidth): an 8 base up-chirp + 2 down-chirp preamble, then one chirp per SF bits (the last group zero padded). *sample_len is the capacity on input and the written count on output. On SW_ERR_OVERFLOW it holds the required count (checked before any synthesis).
  • Demodulation: sw_css_demodulate searches the whole buffer for the first complete preamble (any amount of audio may precede it), estimates fractional timing and frequency offset, then decodes every remaining whole chirp (dechirp + \(2^{SF}\)-point FFT), so trailing noise also becomes bits. It returns packed bytes, and *bit_len is set to a multiple of 8. It returns SW_ERR_SYNC if no preamble is found and SW_ERR_OVERFLOW (with the required bit count) if the buffer is too small.

docs.title: OFDM modem
docs.text:
int sw_ofdm_modulate(const uint8_t* bits, size_t bit_len, sw_config_t cfg,
                     float* samples, size_t* sample_len);
int sw_ofdm_demodulate(const float* samples, size_t sample_len, sw_config_t cfg,
                       uint8_t* bits, size_t* bit_len);
int sw_ofdm_equalized_symbols(const float* samples, size_t sample_len,
                              sw_config_t cfg, float* iq, size_t* num_points);
  • Output length: (2 + ceil(bit_len / bits_per_symbol)) × (N + cp) samples (two Zadoff-Chu preamble symbols). Here bits_per_symbol = data subcarriers × (1 for BPSK, 2 for QPSK), and the last symbol is zero-padded.
  • Demodulation: detection, CFO correction, a preamble-based LS channel and noise estimate, then ZF or MMSE equalization (cfg.equalizer) and hard demapping. Bits are packed, MSB first.
  • sw_ofdm_equalized_symbols: runs the same receiver but returns the equalized data-subcarrier points as interleaved I0,Q0,I1,Q1,... floats. Points are unit energy (BPSK ±1, QPSK (±1±j)/√2). *num_points is a capacity on input. Output beyond the capacity is truncated, which is not an error. Requires cfg.modulation == 1.

docs.title: Synchronization and CFO
docs.text:
int sw_detect_frame(const float* samples, size_t len, sw_config_t cfg,
                    size_t* frame_start, float* snr);
int sw_estimate_cfo(const float* samples, size_t len, sw_config_t cfg,
                    float* cfo_hz);
  • sw_detect_frame: finds the preamble (CSS: normalised up-/down-chirp correlation scored on all 10 preamble chirps, first preamble in the buffer, see math §3.1; OFDM: Schmidl-Cox repetition metric as presence gate, then the earliest strong peak of a normalised matched filter on the known preamble, refined from the preamble's phase slope). It writes the start offset and an SNR estimate in dB, and returns SW_ERR_SYNC if nothing is above threshold. For CSS mode the buffer must hold the whole 10-chirp preamble; the CSS SNR is an in-band estimate.
  • sw_estimate_cfo: Schmidl-Cox estimate over two repeated periods of N + cp samples. It needs len ≥ 2(N + cp), otherwise it returns SW_ERR_SYNC.

docs.title: Real-time audio I/O
docs.text:
int sw_audio_capture_start(sw_config_t cfg, void** handle);
int sw_audio_capture_read(void* handle, float* buffer, size_t count, size_t* read);
int sw_audio_capture_stop(void* handle);

int sw_audio_playback_start(sw_config_t cfg, void** handle);
int sw_audio_playback_write(void* handle, const float* buffer, size_t count);
int sw_audio_playback_stop(void* handle);
  • Each stream uses the default device at cfg.sample_rate (0 = 44100), mono, through miniaudio, with a one-second 16-bit ring buffer.
  • sw_audio_capture_read returns as many samples as are available, up to count, and sets *read.
  • *_stop frees the handle.
  • On Android only the AAudio and OpenSL ES backends are compiled in.

docs.title: Automatic gain control
docs.text:
int sw_agc_create(int sample_rate, float target_rms, void** handle);
int sw_agc_process(void* handle, float* samples, size_t len);   // in place
int sw_agc_get_gain_db(void* handle, float* gain_db);
int sw_agc_reset(void* handle);
int sw_agc_destroy(void* handle);
  • sample_rate must be 8000..192000. target_rms must be in (0, 1], and 0 selects 0.25.
  • Behavior: attack 1 ms, release 100 ms, 10 ms RMS window, gain 0.1–40 (−20 to +32 dB), output peak-limited to full scale. Non-finite input samples become 0.
  • Handles carry a magic tag, so a stale or foreign pointer is rejected with SW_ERR_BAD_PARAM. Do not use a handle after sw_agc_destroy.

docs.title: FFI allocation helpers (exported, not declared in the header)
docs.text: native/src/api/ffi_helpers.c exports float* sw_alloc_float(int n), double* sw_alloc_double(int n), uint8_t* sw_alloc_uint8(int n) (all calloc-based) and void sw_free(void*). They are not declared in soundwave_api.h, and the Dart app does not use them (it allocates with package:ffi's calloc).

docs.title: Minimal example (CSS round trip)
docs.text:
#include "soundwave_api.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    sw_config_t cfg = {0};          /* all defaults: CSS, 44.1 kHz, 19 kHz, 2 kHz, 20 ms */
    const uint8_t msg[] = { 'H', 'i' };
    size_t n = 0;                   /* ask for the size first */
    float probe;
    if (sw_css_modulate(msg, 16, cfg, &probe, &n) != SW_ERR_OVERFLOW) return 1;
    float* pcm = malloc(n * sizeof *pcm);
    if (sw_css_modulate(msg, 16, cfg, pcm, &n) != SW_OK) return 1;

    uint8_t out[64];
    size_t bits = sizeof out * 8;
    int rc = sw_css_demodulate(pcm, n, cfg, out, &bits);
    printf("rc=%d bits=%zu first=%c%c\n", rc, bits, out[0], out[1]);
    free(pcm);
    return rc;
}

A capacity of 0 is fine for the size query: sw_css_modulate only rejects a NULL samples pointer and a zero bit_len, and it reports the required length with SW_ERR_OVERFLOW. A real application wraps msg in a frame (CRC-32 + RS parity), as soundwave-cli and the app's FrameCodec do; see Architecture.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: This document specifies the Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment pipeline for the Soundwave project using GitHub Actions. The pipeline covers quality gates, multi-platform builds, signing, testing, and deployment.

docs.title: 3.1 Quality Gate — .github/workflows/ci.yml
docs.text:
Trigger: Push to any branch, Pull Requests to main

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['*']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  quality-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: flutter pub get

      - name: Analyze Dart code
        run: flutter analyze --fatal-infos

      - name: Check formatting
        run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .

      - name: Run Flutter tests
        run: flutter test --coverage

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Build DSP core (C/C++)
        run: |
          cd native
          cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
          cmake --build build

      - name: Run DSP core tests
        run: |
          cd native/build
          ctest --output-on-failure

docs.title: 3.3 Sign & Deploy — .github/workflows/release.yml
docs.text:
Triggers:

  • Tag push v* — full release: build, sign (when secrets exist), checksum, publish a draft GitHub Release, upload to stores.
  • workflow_dispatch with input dry_run (default true) — builds, packages, signs-if-possible and checksums everything, uploading results only as workflow artifacts. No GitHub Release, store upload or tag is created. A non-dry manual run publishes only when dispatched on a v* tag ref.
gh workflow run release.yml --ref <branch> -f dry_run=true

The meta job resolves the version (v1.2.3 tag → 1.2.3; otherwise <pubspec version>-dryrun.<run number>) and a publish flag that every publishing job checks.

docs.title: Native library bundling
docs.text:
libsoundwave (from native/) ships inside every desktop app, and lib/native/soundwave_native.dart resolves it relative to the executable (Platform.resolvedExecutable):

Platform How it is built Location in the app Loader path Windows ExternalProject in soundwave_app/windows/CMakeLists.txt (part of flutter build windows) soundwave.dll next to soundwave.exe (renamed from CMake's libsoundwave.dll) <exe dir>\soundwave.dll Linux ExternalProject in soundwave_app/linux/CMakeLists.txt (part of flutter build linux) bundle/lib/libsoundwave.so <exe dir>/lib/libsoundwave.so macOS soundwave_app/macos/packaging/embed_native.sh after flutter build macos (universal arm64 + x86_64, install name @rpath/libsoundwave.dylib) soundwave.app/Contents/Frameworks/libsoundwave.dylib <exe dir>/../Frameworks/libsoundwave.dylib

The native/ project is built as an ExternalProject (not add_subdirectory) because its object-library target is also named soundwave, which clashes with the runner executable. Both build.yml and release.yml assert after the build that the library is present in the bundle, exports sw_* symbols and can be loaded (ctypes.CDLL), and that the macOS runner has the @executable_path/../Frameworks rpath and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription.

docs.title: Desktop packages
docs.text:
Platform Runner Artifacts Packaging script Windows windows-latest soundwave-<ver>-windows-x64.zip, soundwave-<ver>-windows-x64.msix soundwave_app/windows/packaging/package.ps1 (Compress-Archive, Windows SDK makeappx; manifest AppxManifest.xml.in declares runFullTrust + microphone) macOS macos-latest soundwave-<ver>-macos-universal.dmg soundwave_app/macos/packaging/sign_and_package.sh (codesign with hardened runtime + Runner/Release.entitlements, hdiutil UDZO, notarytool + stapler) Linux ubuntu-22.04 (glibc 2.35 baseline) soundwave-<ver>-linux-x64.tar.gz, soundwave_<ver>_amd64.deb, Soundwave-<ver>-x86_64.AppImage soundwave_app/linux/packaging/package.sh (tar, dpkg-deb installing to /opt/soundwave + /usr/bin/soundwave, appimagetool 1.9.1) All ubuntu-latest (checksums job) SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.asc (when GPG key set) inline

Flutter version: macOS jobs pin Flutter 3.50.0; Flutter 3.47.8/3.47.9 gen_snapshot aborts with Class with illegal cid (_Rect in widgets/_window_macos.dart) when building the app with the microphone permission gate (#87). Other jobs stay on 3.47.x until android/ moves to AGP ≥ 9.1.1 (required by Flutter 3.50); then all jobs should use one pinned version.

build.yml produces the same desktop packages unsigned (macOS ad-hoc signed) on every main push / app PR, so packaging regressions surface before a tag.

macOS microphone access: Info.plist has NSMicrophoneUsageDescription; Release.entitlements (applied when signing) has com.apple.security.app-sandbox and com.apple.security.device.audio-input. The packaging script fails if the signed app lacks the audio-input entitlement.

docs.title: Signing (all optional; gated on secret presence)
docs.text:
secrets cannot be used in step-level if:, so each job exposes a presence flag in job-level env (e.g. HAS_WINDOWS_CERT: ${{ secrets.WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 != '' }}) and signing steps test that flag. Without secrets the pipeline still succeeds with unsigned packages.

Platform When secrets exist Without secrets Windows signtool (SHA-256, DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp) signs soundwave.exe, soundwave.dll and the MSIX. MSIX Publisher comes from repository variable MSIX_PUBLISHER and must equal the certificate subject. Unsigned zip + unsigned MSIX (MSIX installs only after signing / developer mode sideload). macOS Certificate imported into a temporary keychain; frameworks/dylibs then the app are signed with Developer ID Application + hardened runtime + timestamp; DMG signed, notarized with xcrun notarytool submit --wait and stapled. Keychain deleted afterwards. Ad-hoc signature (codesign -s -), not notarized; Gatekeeper will require right-click → Open. Linux SHA256SUMS detached-signed (SHA256SUMS.asc) with the GPG key and verified. Unsigned SHA256SUMS.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
• checksums flattens all platform artifacts into one release-assets artifact plus SHA256SUMS; deploy-github-release (needs every platform build + checksums, and publish == 'true') creates a draft release from exactly that set.
  • deploy-android (Play Store internal track) and the Snap publish step also require publish == 'true'.
  • Snap packaging runs only once snap/snapcraft.yaml exists (not yet added).

docs.title: 4. Required Secrets
docs.text:
All signing/publishing secrets are optional: when one is missing the corresponding step is skipped with a ::notice:: and unsigned packages are produced. Add them under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions.

Secret Platform Purpose ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 Android Base64-encoded JKS keystore ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD Android Keystore password ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS Android Key alias ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD Android Key password GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT Android Play Store API credentials MACOS_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 macOS Base64 of the Developer ID Application certificate + private key exported as .p12 (base64 -i cert.p12) MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD macOS Password of that .p12 MACOS_NOTARIZATION_APPLE_ID macOS Apple ID email used for notarytool MACOS_NOTARIZATION_TEAM_ID macOS Apple Developer Team ID MACOS_NOTARIZATION_APP_PASSWORD macOS App-specific password for that Apple ID WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 Windows Base64 of the code-signing .pfx ([Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('cert.pfx'))) WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD Windows Password of that .pfx LINUX_GPG_PRIVATE_KEY Linux / all ASCII-armored private key (gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <id>) used to sign SHA256SUMS LINUX_GPG_PASSPHRASE Linux / all Passphrase of that key (empty if none) SNAP_TOKEN Linux Snapcraft store token CODECOV_TOKEN All Codecov upload token Repository variable (not secret) Purpose MSIX_PUBLISHER MSIX Identity/@Publisher; must exactly equal the Windows certificate subject (e.g. CN=PxA Labs, O=PxA Labs, C=IN). Defaults to CN=PxA Labs.

The macOS certificate is detected by the Developer ID Application identity in the .p12; notarization runs only when that identity and all three MACOS_NOTARIZATION_* secrets are present.

docs.title: Soundwave CLI Guide
docs.text: The Soundwave CLI (soundwave-cli) is a developer command-line tool built to generate, analyze, and simulate acoustic signals for the Soundwave ultrasonic communication protocol. It supports three major commands: modulate, demodulate, and simulate.

docs.title: Building the CLI Target
docs.text:
To build the executable, run the following commands in the native directory:

mkdir -p build && cd build
cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build . --target soundwave_cli

This will produce the soundwave-cli executable inside the build folder (with MSVC, in Release/ or Debug/). The CLI is not built for Android.

docs.title: Notes on the current implementation
docs.text:
• Frame format. modulate wraps the text in the app's PHY frame, [CRC-32 LE][payload 1..219 B][RS parity 32 B] (specification). CLI WAVs decode in the app's Import Signal and app recordings decode with demodulate, given the same modem settings (the defaults match the app's).
  • --sf sets the CSS symbol: each chirp carries SF bits and lasts 2^SF / B (SF 6..10; 127.7 ms and 62.6 bit/s raw at the default SF 8, 2 kHz). The chirp duration follows from --sf and --bw; there is no separate option. Pass the same --sf and --bw to modulate and demodulate. Use --ofdm-mod bpsk for BPSK OFDM.
  • --freq / --bw set the CSS chirp and the OFDM band freq ± bw/2 (default 18–20 kHz). An OFDM band that reaches DC, comes within one subcarrier of Nyquist or holds fewer than 4 subcarriers is rejected.
  • demodulate --mode css searches the whole file for the first complete preamble, so any amount of silence, noise or other audio may precede the frame (fixed Nov 2026; before, a frame more than a few milliseconds into the file was usually missed). The DEBUG: sw_detect_frame ... frame_start = N line reports the same start. The CLI demodulates from that start, as the app does.
  • demodulate decodes the first frame found in the file. It prints the payload on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, including a DEBUG: sw_detect_frame ... snr = X dB line with an uncalibrated SNR estimate. The exit code is 0 only if RS decoding and the CRC succeed.
  • simulate sets the noise power from the average power of the whole file, including any silence. It uses an unseeded C rand(), so every run adds the same noise sequence.
  • For repeated measurements over many frames (field recordings or AWGN sweeps), use docs/testing/ber_sweep.py, described in the field test plan.

docs.title: 1. Signal Modulation (modulate)
docs.text: Converts an ASCII text payload into a 16-bit PCM mono 44.1 kHz WAV audio file using Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) or Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: soundwave-cli modulate --mode <css|ofdm> --input "<text>" --output <filename.wav> [options]

docs.title: Required Arguments
docs.text:
• --mode <css|ofdm>: The modulation technique.
  • --input "<text>": The ASCII string to encode (up to 219 bytes).
  • --output <filename.wav>: Destination path for the generated audio file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --sf <sf>: CSS spreading factor, SF bits per chirp (6..10, default 8).
  • --fft <size>: OFDM FFT size (256, 512, 1024, 2048, default 256).
  • --cp <length>: OFDM cyclic prefix length (default 64).
  • --freq <freq_hz>: Carrier frequency in Hz (default 19000.0; OFDM band centre).
  • --bw <bw_hz>: Bandwidth in Hz (default 2000.0; OFDM band = freq ± bw/2).
  • --ofdm-mod <bpsk|qpsk>: OFDM subcarrier mapping (default qpsk).
  • --no-rs: frames without Reed-Solomon parity (the app's enable_rs off).
  • --amp <amplitude>: Transmit peak level (0.0 to 1.0, default 0.8). Every frame peaks at exactly this value (OFDM is peak-normalized per frame, CSS has a constant envelope), so the 16-bit WAV never clips and the CLI does not rescale the samples. The DEBUG: Modulated signal peak amplitude line on stderr reports the peak.

docs.title: CSS Modulation
docs.text: ./soundwave-cli modulate --mode css --input "Hello Soundwave" --output css_frame.wav --sf 8 --freq 19000 --bw 2000

docs.title: OFDM Modulation
docs.text: ./soundwave-cli modulate --mode ofdm --input "Hello OFDM World" --output ofdm_frame.wav --fft 256 --cp 64 --freq 18500

docs.title: 2. Signal Demodulation (demodulate)
docs.text: Reads a WAV audio file, synchronizes the frame, applies frequency offset (CFO) estimation and correction, performs channel equalization, decodes the Reed-Solomon/CRC error correction layers, and outputs the extracted payload to stdout.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: soundwave-cli demodulate --mode <css|ofdm> --input <filename.wav> [options]

docs.title: Required Arguments
docs.text:
• --mode <css|ofdm>: Modulation scheme matching the generated wave.
  • --input <filename.wav>: Input WAV audio file containing the sound wave.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --sf <sf>: CSS spreading factor, SF bits per chirp (6..10, default 8).
  • --fft <size>: OFDM FFT size (default 256).
  • --cp <length>: OFDM cyclic prefix length (default 64).
  • --freq <freq_hz>: Carrier frequency in Hz (default 19000.0; OFDM band centre).
  • --bw <bw_hz>: Bandwidth in Hz (default 2000.0; OFDM band = freq ± bw/2).
  • --ofdm-mod <bpsk|qpsk>: OFDM subcarrier mapping (default qpsk).
  • --no-rs: frames without Reed-Solomon parity (the app's enable_rs off).
  • --equalizer <zf|mmse>: Channel equalization method for OFDM (default zf).

docs.title: Demodulating a CSS Signal
docs.text:
./soundwave-cli demodulate --mode css --input css_frame.wav
Output (stdout, then the last stderr line): 
Hello Soundwave
Demodulation successful! (Errors corrected: 0)

docs.title: Demodulating an OFDM Signal
docs.text:
./soundwave-cli demodulate --mode ofdm --input ofdm_frame.wav --equalizer mmse
Output: 
Hello OFDM World
Demodulation successful! (Errors corrected: 0)

docs.title: 3. AWGN Channel Simulation (simulate)
docs.text: Injects Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) to an input audio wave to model a noisy communication channel at a specified Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) in dB.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: soundwave-cli simulate --input <input.wav> --snr <snr_db> --output <output.wav>

docs.title: Required Arguments
docs.text:
• --input <input.wav>: Clean source WAV file.
  • --snr <snr_db>: Target Signal-to-Noise Ratio in dB. Lower values add more noise.
  • --output <output.wav>: Noisy output WAV file.

docs.title: Add 10 dB SNR AWGN noise to a modulated frame
docs.text:
./soundwave-cli simulate --input css_frame.wav --snr 10 --output noisy_css_frame.wav
Output: 
Successfully simulated AWGN channel on 'css_frame.wav' -> 'noisy_css_frame.wav' (SNR: 10.0 dB)

To verify the robust Reed-Solomon recovery under noise, you can attempt to demodulate the noisy wave: 

./soundwave-cli demodulate --mode css --input noisy_css_frame.wav

docs.title: 2. PHY Frame Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
The app's PHY frame (soundwave_app/lib/engine/frame_codec.dart) is modulated by CSS or OFDM after a mode-specific preamble. CSS uses 8 base up-chirps and 2 down-chirps, then one up-chirp per SF bits; OFDM uses two identical Zadoff-Chu symbols.

graph LR
    P[Preamble<br/>CSS: 8 up + 2 down chirps<br/>OFDM: 2 x ZC symbol] --> C[CRC-32 LE<br/>4 bytes, over payload]
    C --> D[Payload<br/>1..219 bytes]
    D --> R[RS parity<br/>32 bytes, optional]

docs.title: PHY frame format
docs.text:
This is the single frame format of the project. The app (soundwave_app/lib/engine/frame_codec.dart) and soundwave-cli (native/tools/soundwave_cli/frame_format.c) implement it byte for byte:

Field Size Content CRC 4 bytes CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, sw_crc32) over the payload, little-endian Payload 1..219 bytes Application bytes (UTF-8 text, or a link-layer frame) RS parity 32 bytes, unless RS is off (enable_rs / --no-rs) sw_rs_encode over CRC + payload: a shortened RS(255,223) codeword of at most 255 bytes

Example: payload hello gives 86 A6 10 36 68 65 6C 6C 6F followed by 32 parity bytes (native/tests/test_cli_frame.c, soundwave_app/test/native/cli_compat_test.dart).

There is no length field. The demodulator returns every symbol in its input, including noise after the frame, so the receiver tries lengths from the shortest upwards and takes the first one whose RS decode (if enabled) and CRC-32 both verify. This keeps the on-air format of the deployed app and its link layer unchanged. A false accept needs a wrong length to pass both RS decoding and a 32-bit CRC; without RS it needs a CRC-32 collision at one of at most 219 candidate lengths, about \(219 \cdot 2^{-32} \approx 5 \times 10^{-8}\) per frame. A length field would not remove the search for the end of the frame in a stream; it would add two bytes that themselves need protection.

The OFDM modulator additionally whitens the frame bits (PRBS15) on air. That is part of the modem, not of the byte format.

The TX/RX sequence diagrams, threading and persistence are described in the architecture overview. Band, rate and airtime per configuration are in Signal chain & parameters.

docs.title: Link Layer: Fragmentation, File Transfer & ARQ (#89, #100)
docs.text:
Implemented in pure Dart (soundwave_app/lib/engine/): link_frame.dart (formats), fragmentation.dart (fragmenter/reassembler), link_receiver.dart (RX policy), arq.dart (stop-and-wait sender). It runs inside the PHY frame payload ([CRC-32][payload <= 219 B][RS parity], see frame_codec.dart).

Payload discrimination. A PHY payload whose first byte is 0xFA is a link frame; anything else is legacy raw UTF-8 text (0xFA never occurs in UTF-8). Short text with ARQ off is still sent as a legacy frame, so old receivers keep working. Longer text, files, and everything sent with ARQ on use link frames.

Frame Layout (little-endian) Size DATA FA 01 flags src:u16 msgId:u16 index:u16 count:u16 chunk 11 + 1..208 B ACK FA 02 00 src:u16 dst:u16 msgId:u16 index:u16 11 B NACK FA 03 reason src:u16 dst:u16 msgId:u16 index:u16 11 B

flags bit 0 = ACK requested. src/dst are random per-app 16-bit node ids; frames with src equal to the local id are the device hearing its own speaker and are ignored.

Message envelope (what gets fragmented): kind:u8 (1 text, 2 file) | length:u32 | crc32(content):u32 | [file: nameLen:u8 name mimeLen:u8 mime] | content. Content is limited to 1 MiB (about 5,050 fragments). The reassembler delivers a message only when all count fragments are present and the envelope CRC-32 verifies.

Reassembly. Fragments are buffered per (src, msgId) in any order. Duplicates are dropped, and ids that were already delivered are remembered for 10 minutes so retransmissions are not delivered twice. At most 8 concurrent messages are kept (the least recently updated one is evicted). An incomplete message is abandoned after an idle timeout of 30 s + (maxRetries + 2) x (2 x max-frame airtime + largest backoff), and the failure is reported on RxEngine.transfers.

ARQ (stop-and-wait). Only one side can transmit at a time, and frames are long compared with the turnaround, so the sender waits for each fragment's ACK before sending the next. The wait is airtime + responseAllowance + ackTimeout x 2^attempt (+ up to 10 % jitter). responseAllowance is the ACK's airtime plus the RX decode latency, computed from FrameGeometry. A NACK triggers an immediate retransmission. After maxRetries retransmissions of one fragment the transfer fails with TxMaxRetriesError. When a receiver sees a CRC/RS failure while exactly one ARQ transfer is in progress, it NACKs that transfer's lowest missing fragment. Otherwise it stays silent and the sender's timeout covers the loss. Identical replies within 150 ms are debounced, and a genuine retransmission is always ACKed again because it means the earlier ACK was lost.

Settings (arq_enabled default off, arq_max_retries 1/3/5, arq_ack_timeout_ms 200-2000, added on top of the airtime). With ARQ off, fragments are broadcast once, paced by their airtime, and receivers never transmit. With ARQ on, both devices must enable it and listen. The app starts listening automatically before an ARQ file send. Received files are saved under <app documents>/Soundwave/received/ with sanitized, non-overwriting names (services/received_file_store.dart).

docs.title: 3. FFI Memory Ownership Contracts & Buffer Lifecycle
docs.text: When calling C code from Dart via dart:ffi, managing memory safely across the language boundary is paramount to prevent memory leaks and dangling pointer crashes.

docs.title: Memory Rules
docs.text:
1. Caller Allocates, Callee Fills:
  2. The Dart caller (SoundwaveNative) MUST allocate memory buffers using ffi.calloc or ffi.malloc before passing pointers to C functions.

  3. Native C functions write into pre-allocated memory buffers and return written lengths via output parameter pointers (size_t*).

  4. Caller Frees:

  5. Any memory allocated by Dart MUST be freed by Dart using calloc.free(ptr) inside a try ... finally block after the native call completes.

  6. Native C functions in libsoundwave DO NOT retain or free pointers passed to them.

  7. Buffer Length Estimation Formulas:

  8. RS Parity Allocation: \(N_{\text{parity}} = 2t = N_{\text{block}} - K_{\text{data}}\) bytes (default 32 bytes for \(RS(255, 223)\)).
  9. CSS Audio Samples: \(N_{\text{samples}} = (10 + \lceil N_{\text{bits}} / SF \rceil) \times 2^{SF} \times \text{round}(f_s / B)\) floats (10-chirp preamble, one chirp per SF bits). FrameGeometry in lib/engine/frame_geometry.dart mirrors this.
  10. OFDM Audio Samples: \(N_{\text{samples}} = (2 + \lceil N_{\text{bits}} / B_{\text{sym}} \rceil) \times (N_{\text{fft}} + N_{\text{cp}}) + \lfloor N_{\text{cp}}/2 \rfloor\), where \(B_{\text{sym}}\) is the number of data subcarriers in the configured band times bits per subcarrier (see Signal chain).
  11. In practice, call once with a too-small capacity: the API returns SW_ERR_OVERFLOW and writes the required length.

docs.title: Memory Ownership Pattern Example (Dart FFI)
docs.text:
// Example: safe FFI allocation (pattern used in lib/native/soundwave_native.dart)
Pointer<Uint8> dataPtr = calloc<Uint8>(dataLen);
Pointer<Uint8> parityPtr = calloc<Uint8>(32);
Pointer<Size> parityLenPtr = calloc<Size>();

try {
  // Copy Dart list into native memory
  dataPtr.asTypedList(dataLen).setAll(0, dataBytes);

  // Call C API
  int result = _bindings.sw_rs_encode(dataPtr, dataLen, parityPtr, parityLenPtr);
  if (result != 0) throw Exception("RS Encode Failed: $result");

  // Read back native results
  int writtenLen = parityLenPtr.value;
  List<int> parityBytes = parityPtr.asTypedList(writtenLen).toList();
  return parityBytes;
} finally {
  // Free native memory guaranteed
  calloc.free(dataPtr);
  calloc.free(parityPtr);
  calloc.free(parityLenPtr);
}

docs.text:
SoundwaveNative loads libsoundwave from native/build/ (then the legacy build/). Set SOUNDWAVE_LIB=/abs/path/to/libsoundwave.{so,dylib,dll} to pin a specific build, for example a sanitizer build or the one CI produces. test/native/loopback_test.dart runs real TX → audio → RX round trips (CSS and OFDM) against it. Locally it is skipped when no library loads, while CI sets SOUNDWAVE_REQUIRE_NATIVE=1 so a missing library fails the job.

cmake -S native -B native/build -DSW_BUILD_TESTS=OFF && cmake --build native/build --target soundwave_shared
cd soundwave_app && flutter test

docs.title: Android (NDK + AAudio)
docs.text:
No separate native build step is needed: soundwave_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts points Gradle's externalNativeBuild at native/CMakeLists.txt, so flutter build apk / flutter run compiles libsoundwave.so with the NDK (ndkVersion comes from the Flutter SDK) for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 and packages it under lib/<abi>/. Dart loads it with DynamicLibrary.open('libsoundwave.so').

Requirements: Android SDK with NDK and CMake 3.22+ (Gradle installs them on demand once the SDK licenses are accepted), JDK 17.

cd soundwave_app
flutter build apk --debug                      # all ABIs, debug-signed
flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi    # app-<abi>-release.apk
flutter build appbundle --release              # app-release.aab (Play Store)
unzip -l build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-v8a-release.apk | grep libsoundwave.so

Android specifics in the native build:

  • Audio backend: audio_io.c compiles only miniaudio's AAudio and OpenSL ES backends. AAudio is used on API 26+, OpenSL ES is the fallback. Both use the low-latency performance profile and the unprocessed input preset, because the default voice presets apply AGC, noise suppression and low-pass filtering that remove the 18–22 kHz band.
  • SIMD: NEON is required (SW_REQUIRE_NEON, a compile error otherwise) on arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a. x86_64 uses SSE4.2 and never AVX2, which the Android x86_64 ABI does not guarantee.
  • Linking: m dl log, a 16 KB page-aligned ELF (needed for Play Store uploads targeting Android 15+), and no versioned SONAME.
  • Permissions: the manifest declares RECORD_AUDIO and MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS. On first launch, MicPermissionGate explains why the microphone is needed and then shows the system prompt. NativeAudioService.startCapture() checks the permission again and throws MicrophonePermissionDenied if it is missing.

Release signing: create soundwave_app/android/key.properties (it is gitignored) with storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias and keyPassword. storeFile is relative to android/app/. Without that file, release builds are debug-signed. In CI, the build-android job in build.yml writes the file from the ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 (base64 of the .jks), ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS and ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secrets when they are set. The job uploads android-debug-apk, android-release-apks and android-release-aab. It fails if libsoundwave.so is missing for any ABI, if the expected sw_* symbols are not exported, or if the 64-bit .so is not 16 KB aligned. To run it on a branch, use gh workflow run build.yml --ref <branch>.

docs.title: Sanitizers & Fuzzing
docs.text:
The DSP core treats every sw_* call as a trust boundary: Dart passes user-controlled settings and microphone samples straight into C. Sanitizer and fuzzing support is built in (issue #28).

CMake option Default Effect SW_ENABLE_ASAN OFF AddressSanitizer (+LeakSanitizer on Linux). GCC/Clang: -fsanitize=address; MSVC: /fsanitize=address SW_ENABLE_UBSAN OFF UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, fatal on the first report. With Clang it also traps float division by zero, which in DSP code signals a missing guard SW_ENABLE_FUZZER OFF Builds the native/Fuzzing/ harnesses as real libFuzzer binaries (needs LLVM Clang; AppleClang has no libFuzzer) SW_FUZZ_SMOKE ON Builds the same harnesses with a standalone driver and registers them in CTest as fuzz_*_smoke (SW_FUZZ_SMOKE_RUNS random inputs each) SW_USE_SANITIZER, SW_BUILD_FUZZ OFF Deprecated aliases for ASan+UBSan and SW_ENABLE_FUZZER 
cd native
cmake --preset asan  && cmake --build build/asan  && ctest --test-dir build/asan  --output-on-failure
cmake --preset ubsan && cmake --build build/ubsan && ctest --test-dir build/ubsan --output-on-failure

# libFuzzer (Linux, or macOS with Homebrew LLVM)
cmake --preset fuzz && cmake --build build/fuzz
./build/fuzz/Fuzzing/fuzz_api -max_total_time=60

Harnesses (native/Fuzzing/). Each one checks properties, not just "no crash":

  • fuzz_crc: the table, fast and FFI CRC paths agree, and every 1-bit error is detected.
  • fuzz_rs: arbitrary words decode only to valid codewords, and encode→corrupt(≤16)→decode restores the message with the exact error count.
  • fuzz_packet, fuzz_fec: decoding arbitrary bytes is safe, and encode→decode round-trips.
  • fuzz_css, fuzz_ofdm: raw samples (NaN/Inf/huge) through the internal entry points and the FFI wrappers.
  • fuzz_api: every sw_* function with fuzzed configs and exact-capacity output buffers. It includes modulate→perturb→demodulate round trips so deep demodulator paths get exercised.

Reproducing a CI crash. Download the crash-<target> artifact and replay it. The same command works with the libFuzzer and the smoke builds:

./build/asan/Fuzzing/fuzz_api path/to/crash-<sha1>

macOS note. On some macOS releases the AppleClang ASan runtime hangs during start-up. Homebrew LLVM works: configure with -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang++, which also gives you libFuzzer on macOS. When ASan is off, the CTest fuzz smoke tests on macOS automatically run under Guard Malloc (libgmalloc), which puts every allocation against a guard page so heap overruns still fault.

Canaries. In ASan builds, asan_trigger_* tests make deliberate overflow, use-after-free and (Linux) leak errors. They pass only when the sanitizer report appears, so a green run proves the sanitizer is actually active.

Static analysis. CI runs cppcheck (native/.cppcheck-suppressions) and clang-tidy (native/.clang-tidy). Clang Static Analyzer findings fail the build; bugprone/CERT checks are advisory.

docs.text:

  • Doxygen Documentation: All public functions in soundwave_api.h MUST have Doxygen docstrings (/** ... */).

docs.title: Soundwave: Physical Layer Mathematical Model
docs.text: This document outlines the rigorous mathematical and physical formulations governing the physical layer (PHY) of the Soundwave communication system. Soundwave transmits digital data over short distances using ultrasonic acoustic waves (typically \(18 \text{ kHz}\) to \(22 \text{ kHz}\)) using consumer-grade speakers and microphones.

docs.title: 1. Acoustic Wave Propagation & Channel Modeling
docs.text: Acoustic transmission differs significantly from radio frequency (RF) propagation due to the slow speed of sound (\(c \approx 343 \text{ m/s}\) at \(20^\circ\text{C}\) in air) and high attenuation in the ultrasonic range.

docs.title: 1.1 The Acoustic Wave Equation
docs.text:
In a homogeneous, lossless fluid medium, acoustic pressure waves \(p(\mathbf{r}, t)\) satisfy the three-dimensional wave equation:

\[\nabla^2 p(\mathbf{r}, t) - \frac{1}{c^2} \frac{\partial^2 p(\mathbf{r}, t)}{\partial t^2} = 0\]

where: - \(\nabla^2\) is the Laplacian operator. - \(\mathbf{r} = [x, y, z]^T\) represents the spatial coordinates. - \(c\) is the speed of sound.

docs.title: 1.2 Frequency-Dependent Attenuation (Path Loss)
docs.text:
Sound propagation in air experiences frequency-dependent attenuation due to classical viscosity, thermal conduction, and molecular relaxation of Nitrogen (\(N_2\)) and Oxygen (\(O_2\)). The attenuation coefficient \(\alpha(f)\) in \(\text{dB/m}\) can be approximated via Stokes' Law of sound attenuation at high frequencies:

\[\alpha(f) \approx \frac{8\pi^2 \eta}{3 \rho_0 c^3} f^2\]

where: - \(\eta\) is the dynamic viscosity of air. - \(\rho_0\) is the ambient density of air. - \(f\) is the carrier frequency.

The total path loss \(A(d, f)\) over a distance \(d\) (meters) for a signal with frequency \(f\) is modeled as:

\[A(d, f) = d^{-\gamma} \cdot e^{-\alpha(f) d}\]

where \(\gamma\) is the path loss exponent (\(\gamma = 2\) for free-space spherical wave spreading, and \(\gamma < 2\) in indoor waveguide-like corridors).

docs.title: 1.3 Multipath Channel Impulse Response (CIR)
docs.text:
Indoor acoustic channels are highly reverberant. The channel impulse response \(h(t)\) is represented as a discrete tapped delay line:

\[h(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{L-1} a_i(t) \delta(t - \tau_i(t))\]

where: - \(L\) is the number of resolvable propagation paths. - \(a_i(t)\) is the time-varying path amplitude. - \(\tau_i(t)\) is the time-varying path delay. - \(\delta(t)\) is the Dirac delta function.

The corresponding frequency response (transfer function) is:

\[H(f, t) = \sum_{i=0}^{L-1} a_i(t) e^{-j 2\pi f \tau_i(t)}\]

docs.title: 1.4 Doppler Scaling Effect
docs.text:
Since the speed of sound \(c\) is small, even slow relative motion between the transmitter and receiver creates significant Doppler shifts. The received signal \(y(t)\) subject to a relative velocity \(v\) is scaled in time:

\[y(t) = x\left( (1 + \beta) t - \tau_0 \right)\]

where: - \(\beta = \frac{v}{c}\) is the Doppler scaling factor. - \(\tau_0\) is the initial propagation delay.

The frequency shifts to:

\[f_{rx} = f_{tx} (1 + \beta)\]

docs.title: 2. Modulation Schemes
docs.text: Soundwave supports two physical layer modulation options: Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) for robustness at low rates, and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) for high throughput.

docs.title: 2.1 Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS)
docs.text: CSS in Soundwave uses LoRa-style chirp symbols: every data symbol is the same linear up-chirp, cyclically shifted in frequency, so one chirp carries \(SF\) bits. Implementation: native/src/css/css_modulate.c (transmitter) and native/src/css/css_demodulate.c (receiver).

docs.title: 2.1.1 Parameters and sampling
docs.text:
Symbol Meaning Config field / default \(f_s\) sample rate sample_rate, 44 100 Hz \(f_c\) band centre carrier_freq, 19 000 Hz \(SF\) spreading factor, \(6 \le SF \le 10\) sf, 8 \(M = 2^{SF}\) chips per symbol (and symbol alphabet size) \(D = \operatorname{round}(f_s / B_{cfg})\) samples per chip, \(D \ge 1\) from bandwidth (2000 Hz) \(B = f_s / D\) effective sweep bandwidth \(N = M D\) samples per symbol \(T = M / B = N / f_s\) symbol duration

The configured bandwidth is quantised to \(f_s / D\) so that a chip is a whole number of samples and every symbol is exactly \(N = MD\) samples. At 44.1 kHz, bandwidth 2000 gives \(D = 22\), \(B = 2004.5\) Hz; 4000 gives \(D = 11\), \(B = 4009.1\) Hz. The receiver works at the chip rate \(B\) after filtering, so \(D\) is the oversampling factor of the audio stream. symbol_duration is not used by CSS: the symbol length follows from \(SF\) and \(B\). The band \([f_c - B/2, f_c + B/2]\) must lie in \((0, f_s/2]\); otherwise the configuration is rejected (SW_ERR_BAD_PARAM).

docs.title: 2.1.2 Symbol waveform
docs.text:
Symbol value \(k \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}\) is the base up-chirp started \(k\) chips into its sweep. Its instantaneous frequency is

\[f_k(t) = f_c - \frac{B}{2} + B \left( \frac{k}{M} + \frac{t}{T} \bmod 1 \right), \qquad 0 \le t < T,\]

that is, it starts at \(f_c - B/2 + kB/M\), rises at \(B/T\) Hz/s and wraps from \(f_c + B/2\) back to \(f_c - B/2\) at \(t_w = T(1 - k/M)\), which is sample \((M - k) D\). The transmitted sample is \(s[n] = A \cos(2\pi \varphi(n / f_s))\) with \(\varphi\) the integral of \(f_k\) and \(A\) = amplitude \(\in (0, 1]\), so \(\max_n |s[n]| \le A\) (constant envelope); phase is carried across symbols so the signal is continuous. The down-chirp used in the preamble sweeps \(f_c + B/2 \to f_c - B/2\).

docs.title: 2.1.3 Bits to symbols (Gray mapping) and frame
docs.text:
Bits are taken MSB first, \(SF\) at a time (the last group is zero padded). A group with value \(v\) is sent as the symbol \(k\) whose Gray code equals \(v\), i.e. \(v = k \oplus (k \gg 1)\). The most likely demodulation error is a neighbouring bin (\(k \pm 1\), also across the wrap \(M-1 \leftrightarrow 0\)), and neighbours differ in exactly one bit. A frame is

\[\underbrace{8 \times \text{base up-chirp } (k = 0)}_{\text{preamble}} \;\; \underbrace{2 \times \text{down-chirp}}_{\text{sync word}} \;\; \underbrace{\lceil n_{bits} / SF \rceil \times \text{data up-chirps}}_{\text{payload}}\]

so it occupies \((10 + \lceil n_{bits}/SF \rceil) \cdot N\) samples. Data symbols are always up-chirps; a payload can therefore contain base up-chirps (e.g. zero bytes) but never a down-chirp.

docs.title: 2.1.4 Demodulation (dechirp + FFT)
docs.text:
1. Complex baseband. \(z[n] = \text{LPF}\{ y[n] e^{-j 2\pi f_c n / f_s} \}\) with a Hamming-windowed sinc low-pass of \(10D + 1\) taps and cut-off \(0.6B\). It removes the negative-frequency image at \(-2f_c\) and the noise outside the band; its group delay is compensated so \(z\) is aligned with \(y\).
  2. Chip samples. For data symbol \(i\) starting at \(t_i = \hat{t}_0 + (10 + i) N\) (fractional), take \(z\) at \(t_i + mD\), \(m = 0, \dots, M-1\) (linear interpolation), and remove the estimated frequency offset: \(v[m] = z(t_i + mD)\, e^{-j 2\pi \widehat{\Delta f} (t_i + mD)/f_s}\).
  3. Dechirp. Multiply by the conjugate chip-rate base chirp \(c[m] = e^{j\pi(m^2/M - m)}\). Symbol \(k\) becomes a tone of \(k/M\) cycles per chip; at the chip rate the wrapped part of the chirp aliases onto the same tone.
  4. FFT and decision. \(\hat{k} = \arg\max_k |\mathrm{FFT}_M\{v[m] c^*[m]\}[k]|^2\), then \(v = \hat{k} \oplus (\hat{k} \gg 1)\) gives the \(SF\) bits.

The decision is a bank of \(M\) matched filters computed by one \(M\)-point FFT. Integrating \(M\) chips gives a processing gain of \(10 \log_{10} M\) dB (18.1 dB at SF6, 30.1 dB at SF10).

docs.title: 2.1.5 Valid SF range (computed, 44.1 kHz)
docs.text:
\(SF\) \(N\) at 2 kHz (\(D\)=22) \(T\) at 2 kHz Raw rate at 2 kHz \(N\) at 4 kHz (\(D\)=11) \(T\) at 4 kHz Raw rate at 4 kHz Bin spacing \(B/M\) at 4 kHz 6 1408 31.9 ms 187.9 bit/s 704 16.0 ms 375.9 bit/s 62.6 Hz 7 2816 63.9 ms 109.6 bit/s 1408 31.9 ms 219.2 bit/s 31.3 Hz 8 (default) 5632 127.7 ms 62.6 bit/s 2816 63.9 ms 125.3 bit/s 15.7 Hz 9 11264 255.4 ms 35.2 bit/s 5632 127.7 ms 70.5 bit/s 7.8 Hz 10 22528 510.8 ms 19.6 bit/s 11264 255.4 ms 39.2 bit/s 3.9 Hz

Raw rate \(= SF \cdot B / M\) (computed from the formulas above, not measured; preamble and FEC excluded). At 2 kHz the bin spacing is half the 4 kHz value.

Why \(6 \le SF \le 10\):

  • Upper bound. A frequency error of half a bin moves the FFT peak to the wrong symbol. The preamble estimate below removes a static offset, but what changes during a frame is not tracked: a speaker/microphone clock mismatch of ±50 ppm per device is up to 2 Hz at 20 kHz, and 0.1 m/s of hand movement is a 5.5 Hz Doppler shift at 19 kHz. At SF10 the bin is already 3.9 Hz (4 kHz band) or 2.0 Hz (2 kHz band); SF11/12 would be 1–2 Hz (0.5–1 Hz at 2 kHz) with 0.5–2 s symbols. Symbols are also capped at 1 s (CSS_MAX_SYMBOL_SEC), which SF11 already exceeds at 2 kHz.
  • Lower bound. Below SF6 the processing gain is under 18 dB and the preamble correlation of noise or data (\(\approx 1/M\), see 3.1) gets close to the detection threshold.
  • Oversampling. For any \(B \le f_s/2\), \(D = \operatorname{round}(f_s/B) \ge 2\) samples per chip. The symbol is an integer number of samples for every SF, so no fractional resampling is needed.

docs.title: 2.1.6 FEC
docs.text: CSS and OFDM share the frame FEC: Reed-Solomon RS(255,223) with 32 parity bytes (corrects 16 byte errors), on or off. There is no adjustable code rate; the former coding_rate setting had no effect and was removed from the app. The sw_config_t.coding_rate field remains for ABI compatibility and is ignored.

docs.title: 2.2 Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM)
docs.text: For high-rate communications, OFDM divides the transmission band into \(N_c\) orthogonal subcarriers.

docs.title: 2.2.1 Transmitted Signal Formulation
docs.text:
The baseband complex OFDM symbol \(x(t)\) is formulated as:

\[x(t) = \sum_{k=0}^{N_c - 1} X_k e^{j 2\pi k \Delta f t}, \quad 0 \leq t \leq T_{sub}\]

where: - \(X_k\) is the complex modulation symbol (e.g., BPSK, QPSK, or QAM) mapped to the \(k\)-th subcarrier. - \(\Delta f = \frac{1}{T_{sub}}\) is the subcarrier spacing (ensuring orthogonality). - \(T_{sub}\) is the active symbol duration.

To eliminate Inter-Symbol Interference (ISI) caused by multipath delay spread, a Cyclic Prefix (CP) of duration \(T_{cp} > \max(\tau_i)\) is prepended, yielding the full symbol duration \(T_{sym} = T_{sub} + T_{cp}\):

\[x_{cp}(t) = \begin{cases} x(t + T_{sub} - T_{cp}), & 0 \leq t < T_{cp} \\ x(t - T_{cp}), & T_{cp} \leq t \leq T_{sym} \end{cases}\]

docs.title: 2.2.2 Discrete-Time Processing (IDFT/DFT)
docs.text:
Using a digital processor, modulation is performed using the Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT):

\[x[n] = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} X_k e^{j \frac{2\pi k n}{N}}, \quad 0 \leq n \leq N-1\]

And demodulation extracts the subcarriers via the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) at the receiver:

\[Y_k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} y[n + N_{cp} - b] e^{-j \frac{2\pi k n}{N}}, \quad b = \lfloor N_{cp} / 4 \rfloor\]

The FFT window starts \(b\) samples inside the cyclic prefix rather than at its end (see section 4.0 for why).

docs.title: 2.2.3 Ultrasonic Band Plan
docs.text:
The audio is real, so \(X_{N-k} = X_k^*\) and only bins \(1 \le k \le N/2 - 1\) are chosen freely. Bin \(k\) sits at \(f_k = k f_s / N\). The occupied band is set by carrier_freq \(f_c\) and bandwidth \(B\) (defaults 19 kHz and 2 kHz, i.e. 18–20 kHz):

\[K_a = \{k_{lo}, \dots, k_{hi}\}, \quad k_{lo} = \left\lceil \frac{(f_c - B/2) N}{f_s} \right\rceil + 1, \quad k_{hi} = \left\lfloor \frac{(f_c + B/2) N}{f_s} \right\rfloor - 1\]

The \(+1\) / \(-1\) leave one empty guard bin inside each band edge, so the main lobe of the outermost subcarrier stays (almost entirely) inside the band. Every bin outside \(K_a\) (DC, the whole audible range, Nyquist) is zero on transmit, and the receiver uses only \(K_a\) for timing, CFO, channel and noise estimation, equalization and demapping. A configuration is rejected unless \(f_c - B/2 > 0\), \(f_c + B/2 \le f_s/2 - f_s/N\) (one subcarrier spacing of guard below Nyquist) and \(|K_a| \ge 4\). Every 8th active bin, starting with \(k_{lo}\), is a pilot with value \(+1, -1, +1, \dots\); the other \(|K_a| - \lceil |K_a|/8 \rceil\) bins carry data, so one OFDM symbol carries \((|K_a| - \lceil |K_a|/8 \rceil) \cdot m\) bits with \(m = 1\) (BPSK) or \(2\) (QPSK). The code is ofdm_layout_compute (C) and OfdmBand (Dart), which use the same arithmetic.

Transmit windowing. A rectangular symbol has a sinc spectrum whose \(1/f^2\) power sidelobes leave roughly \(-26\) dB of the frame energy below 16 kHz even when every active bin is above 18 kHz. Each symbol therefore rises with a raised-cosine ramp \(r[n] = \tfrac12\left(1 - \cos\frac{\pi (n + 1/2)}{W}\right)\) over its first \(W = \lfloor N_{cp}/2 \rfloor\) samples, while the previous symbol continues with its cyclic suffix (its first \(W\) body samples) weighted by \(r[W-1-n]\). Because \(r[n] + r[W-1-n] = 1\) the cross-fade has unit gain. It lies inside the cyclic prefix, before the receiver's FFT window (which starts at \(N_{cp} - b \ge W\)), so it costs no throughput; the frame only grows by the last symbol's fade-out:

\[\text{samples} = (2 + N_{sym}) (N + N_{cp}) + \lfloor N_{cp}/2 \rfloor\]

The two preamble copies are joined without a cross-fade so that they stay sample-identical (section 3). To keep that one junction continuous anyway, the preamble's ZC sequence is multiplied by the common phase \(e^{j\varphi}\) for which \(\text{Re}\{e^{j\varphi}(z[N - N_{cp}] - z[0])\} = 0\), with \(z[n] = \sum_{k \in K_a} X_k e^{j 2\pi k n / N}\): the first sample of the second copy's prefix then equals the natural continuation of the first copy.

Data whitening. With only a few data bins (8 at \(N = 256\) in the default band, i.e. 16 bits per QPSK symbol), repeated payload bytes would produce identical consecutive OFDM symbols, which a repetition detector cannot tell from the preamble. Data bits are therefore XORed with the PRBS15 sequence \(x^{15} + x^{14} + 1\) (seed all ones, restarted every frame, ofdm_scramble) before mapping and after demapping. The zero padding that fills the last symbol is whitened too: left constant, it would put the same point on every padded subcarrier, a coherent pulse with a crest factor of up to about 26 dB (see Transmit level). The receiver descrambles every demodulated bit, so padding still decodes as zeros.

Transmit level. A sum of \(2|K_a|\) unit-magnitude subcarriers has RMS \(\sqrt{2|K_a|/N}\) per sample (about 0.28–0.30 in the default band) but a peak that depends on \(N\), the band and the data, so the raw IDFT output can exceed full scale (raw peaks of about 1–3 in the default band and up to about 6 in wider bands, crest factors 9–19 dB; native/tests/test_tx_peak.c prints them). Clipping at the DAC would spread energy over the whole spectrum, including the audible band. The modulator therefore scales the whole frame by one gain

\[g = \frac{A}{\max_n |x[n]|}, \qquad A = \texttt{amplitude} \in (0, 1]\]

(ofdm_peak_normalize), so the transmitted peak is exactly \(A\) and the spectrum shape is unchanged. A real gain common to the whole frame is a flat channel: the receiver's preamble channel estimate absorbs it, so the equalized points are still unit-energy constellation points. The price is that the RMS level is \(A\) divided by the frame's crest factor, which also varies a little from frame to frame. Peak-to-average power reduction (e.g. tone reservation on unused in-band bins) could raise the RMS level for the same peak; it is not implemented.

native/tests/test_ofdm_spectrum.c computes the transmit spectrum of a typical frame and requires at least 98.5 % of the energy in \([f_c - B/2, f_c + B/2]\) and at most \(-40\) dB below 16 kHz for every tested FFT size. The values it prints are listed in Signal chain & parameters.

docs.title: 3. Synchronization & Frame Detection
docs.text: Proper timing and frequency synchronization are critical in acoustic communication to align the receiver's decoding window and correct for carrier frequency offsets.

docs.title: 3.1 CSS Preamble Detection
docs.text:
The CSS receiver (css_detect_frame() in native/src/css/css_demodulate.c; sync_detect_frame() mode 0 and sw_detect_frame() call it) searches the whole buffer on the complex baseband \(z[n]\) of section 2.1.4. For every lag \(m\) it correlates the \(N\)-sample window with the base up-chirp \(u[n]\) and with the down-chirp \(u^*[n]\) (FFT overlap-save, \(O(L \log N)\)):

\[c_{up}[m] = \frac{1}{N}\left| \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} z[m+n]\, u^*[n] \right|^2, \qquad c_{dn}[m] = \frac{1}{N}\left| \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} z[m+n]\, u[n] \right|^2.\]

A preamble starting at \(m\) has slots \(m + iN\), \(i = 0..9\). With \(\bar{E}(m)\) the mean window energy \(\sum_n |z|^2\) of those 10 slots, it scores

\[U(m) = \frac{1}{8 \bar{E}(m)} \sum_{i=0}^{7} c_{up}[m + iN], \qquad D(m) = \frac{\min\left(c_{dn}[m + 8N],\ c_{dn}[m + 9N]\right)}{\bar{E}(m)}.\]

By Cauchy-Schwarz both are at most 1 for a real preamble (equal energy in every slot), whatever the signal level. Normalising by the mean of all 10 slots rather than each slot's own energy means a slot holding only a fragment of signal (a preamble cut by the buffer end, a frame next to silence) cannot score like a whole chirp. Taking the weaker down slot stops a lock one symbol early or late, where one of the two slots holds an up-chirp. Candidates whose slots average more than 60 dB below the loudest window are ignored.

Only lags with the whole 10-chirp preamble inside the buffer are scored, so a preamble near the end of the buffer is not judged on part of its chirps.

  • Threshold. In noise, \(\rho \approx 1/(1.2M)\) (the low-pass passes about \(1.2M\) complex degrees of freedom per window). Detection needs \(U \ge \gamma\) and \(\max_{|\delta| \le 2D} D(m+\delta) \ge \gamma\) with \(\gamma = \min(0.5, 4\theta/M)\) and \(\theta\) = threshold (default 3), i.e. 12/M: 0.19 at SF6, 0.012 at SF10. With \(\rho \approx \text{SNR}_{band}/(1+\text{SNR}_{band})\) this corresponds to an in-band SNR of about −6 dB (SF6) to −19 dB (SF10).
  • Why data cannot fake it. Data symbols are up-chirps only. A shifted up-chirp correlated with the down-chirp template gives \(\rho \approx 1/(2M)\) (stationary-phase estimate), the same order as noise, so the two-down-chirp term stays below \(\gamma\) inside any payload, including payloads of zero bytes (runs of base up-chirps). The old waveform sent a down-chirp for every 1 bit, so the old 8-up/2-down preamble could occur inside data.
  • Peak selection. The start is the maximum of \(U + D\) within one symbol after the first lag that passes. A later, stronger frame in the same buffer is not preferred over the first one.
  • Fractional timing and offset. A frequency offset \(\Delta f\) delays the up-chirp correlation peak and advances the down-chirp peak by \(\Delta f / (B/T)\) seconds, i.e. one chip per bin. With \(t_{up}\), \(t_{dn}\) the parabola-refined peaks of \(U\) and \(D\) within \(\pm 2D\) samples,
\[\hat{t}_0 = \frac{t_{up} + t_{dn}}{2}, \qquad \widehat{\Delta f} = \frac{t_{dn} - t_{up}}{2} \cdot \frac{B}{N} \text{ Hz}.\]

The data symbols are demodulated at the fractional start \(\hat{t}_0\) with \(\widehat{\Delta f}\) removed (offsets up to about ±2 bins). sw_detect_frame reports \(\operatorname{round}(\hat{t}_0)\) and the in-band SNR estimate \(10\log_{10}(\bar\rho / (1 - \bar\rho))\), where \(\bar\rho\) is the preamble mean.

docs.title: 3.2 Zadoff-Chu Sequences for OFDM Sync
docs.text:
For OFDM, a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence is placed in the preamble. ZC sequences possess constant amplitude and zero autocorrelation properties. The \(u\)-th root ZC sequence of length \(N_{ZC}\) (where \(N_{ZC}\) is prime) is defined as:

\[x_u[n] = e^{-j \frac{\pi u n(n+1)}{N_{ZC}}}, \quad 0 \leq n < N_{ZC}\]

The preamble uses root \(u = 1\) with \(N_{ZC} = |K_a|\) on the active bins (section 2.2.3), sent twice. Coarse timing is the Schmidl-Cox repetition metric over the period \(L = N + N_{cp}\), computed on the analytic signal. With a narrow band that peak is broad, so it is refined from the preamble itself. A window that starts \(s\) samples away from the symbol body gives \(Y_k = H_k X_k e^{j 2\pi k s / N}\), so with \(D_k = (Y_{k+1} X_{k+1}^*)(Y_k X_k^*)^*\) summed over adjacent active bins of both copies,

\[\hat{s} = \frac{N}{2\pi} \angle \sum_k D_k, \qquad \hat{\delta} = \hat{s} + b\]

and the frame start is moved by \(-\operatorname{round}(\hat{\delta})\) (two passes, ofdm_refine_timing). The same sums give a preamble score \(|\sum_k D_k| / \sum_k |D_k|\): close to 1 for the real preamble, about \(1/\sqrt{|K_a|}\) for anything else. A Schmidl-Cox candidate that scores below 0.5 (some other repetition) is re-checked with a matched filter on the known two-copy preamble, and the better-scoring start is used (ofdm_locate_preamble).

docs.title: 3.3 Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) Estimation
docs.text:
A frequency offset \(\Delta f_c\) introduces a phase rotation in the received samples:

\[y[n] = x[n] e^{j 2\pi \frac{\Delta f_c}{f_s} n}\]

Using Schmidl-Cox sync with two identical consecutive training symbols of period \(N\), the CFO is estimated by checking the phase angle of the autocorrelation:

\[\Delta \hat{f}_c = \frac{f_s}{2\pi N} \angle \left( \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} y^*[n] y[n + N] \right)\]

In the OFDM receiver the two training symbols are the two identical preamble symbols, each with its cyclic prefix, so the repetition period is \(L = N + N_{cp}\). The receiver evaluates the correlation in the frequency domain, on the same FFT windows that the channel estimate uses (section 4.0):

\[\Delta \hat{f}_c = \frac{f_s}{2\pi L} \angle \left( \sum_{k \in K_a} Y_1^*[k] \, Y_2[k] \right)\]

A frequency offset rotates each active subcarrier of the second copy by \(e^{j 2\pi \Delta f_c L / f_s}\) relative to the first. Both windows lie inside the repeated preamble for every timing error the receiver tolerates, so a noiseless frame gives exactly \(\Delta \hat{f}_c = 0\). The time-domain sum over a full window of \(L\) samples does not have this property. With a timing error of \(\delta\) samples, \(|\delta|\) samples of that window fall outside the repetition and bias the estimate. Because the signal is real, its mirror-image spectrum leaks into the active band, and the leakage grows with the offset. The estimate is therefore run twice: the second pass estimates the small residual left after correcting with the first estimate, and the two are added.

The received audio is real, so the timing metric and the CFO correction run on its analytic signal \(z[n]\). It is formed over a buffer of length \(M\) with the DFT:

\[Z[k] = \begin{cases} X[k], & k = 0 \text{ or } k = M/2 \ (M \text{ even}) \\ 2X[k], & 0 < k < M/2 \\ 0, & M/2 < k < M \end{cases}\]

so that \(\text{Re}\{z[n]\} = x[n]\) exactly, and the CFO-corrected real signal is \(\text{Re}\{z[n] e^{-j 2\pi \Delta\hat{f}_c n / f_s}\}\). Both the real and imaginary parts of each positive-frequency bin must be doubled. Doubling only the real part gives \(Z[k] = 2\,\text{Re}\,X[k] + j\,\text{Im}\,X[k]\), whose real part is \(\tfrac{3}{4}x[n] + \tfrac{1}{4}x[(-n) \bmod M]\). That adds a 25 % time-reversed copy of the whole buffer to the signal, which held the noiseless OFDM loopback EVM at about 28 to 45 %.

docs.title: 4.0 Receiver Timing and FFT Window Placement
docs.text:
Let the detected frame start be off by \(\delta\) samples, so that each symbol's FFT window starts at \(N_{cp} - b + \delta\) into the symbol. While \(-(N_{cp} - b) \le \delta \le b\), the window stays inside the current symbol plus its own cyclic prefix. It is then a cyclic shift of the transmitted block (ignoring multipath for this argument):

\[Y_k = H_k X_k \, e^{-j \frac{2\pi k (b - \delta)}{N}}\]

The ramp is the same for the preamble and every data symbol, so it is part of the channel estimate \(\hat{H}[k]\) and is removed exactly by equalization. The first \(W = \lfloor N_{cp}/2 \rfloor\) samples of each symbol hold the transmit cross-fade (section 2.2.3), so the ISI-free range is \(-(N_{cp} - b - W) \le \delta \le b\), i.e. \(\pm N_{cp}/4\) with these defaults; fine timing (section 3.2) keeps \(\delta\) near 0. A data symbol is demodulated when its whole FFT window lies inside the received buffer, so a buffer that ends at the frame's last sample yields every symbol. If \(\delta > b\) (the window is late), it takes \(\delta - b\) samples from the next symbol's cyclic prefix. That causes ISI and inter-carrier interference that no equalizer can remove: in a noiseless loopback, a window just one sample late already gives about 20 % EVM. The Schmidl-Cox timing peak of section 3 can land one or two samples off, so the receiver samples \(b = \lfloor N_{cp}/4 \rfloor\) samples early. The cost is that the multipath delay spread the CP can absorb drops from \(N_{cp}\) to \(N_{cp} - b\).

docs.title: 4.1 Channel Estimation
docs.text:
The channel is estimated from the two identical Zadoff-Chu preamble symbols (section 3.2), which occupy every active subcarrier \(k \in K_a\). Let \(Y_1[k]\) and \(Y_2[k]\) be their DFTs and \(X_{ZC}[k]\) the known preamble values. The Least Squares (LS) estimate averages the two copies:

\[\hat{H}_{LS}[k] = \frac{Y_1[k] + Y_2[k]}{2 X_{ZC}[k]}, \quad k \in K_a\]

Data subcarriers lie inside \(K_a\), so they need no interpolation. Linear interpolation (chanest_linear_interp) only extends \(\hat{H}\) to the guard and null bins:

\[\hat{H}[k] = \text{Interpolate}\left(\hat{H}_{LS}[k_a]\right)\]

The two copies differ only by noise, \(Y_1 - Y_2 = W_1 - W_2\), which gives the per-subcarrier noise variance:

\[\hat{\sigma}_n^2 = \frac{1}{2|K_a|} \sum_{k \in K_a} \left| Y_1[k] - Y_2[k] \right|^2\]

docs.title: 4.2 Equalization
docs.text:
To recover the transmitted data symbol \(X_k\), we apply equalization to correct for the channel frequency response \(\hat{H}[k]\):

  • Zero-Forcing (ZF) Equalizer (simple, but amplifies noise in deep fades): $\(\hat{X}_k = \frac{Y_k}{\hat{H}[k]}\)$

  • Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) Equalizer (balances noise enhancement and channel distortion): $\(\hat{X}_k = \frac{Y_k \hat{H}^*[k]}{|\hat{H}[k]|^2 + \frac{\sigma_n^2}{\sigma_s^2}}\)$

where \(\frac{\sigma_n^2}{\sigma_s^2}\) is the inverse Signal-to-Noise Ratio (\(\text{SNR}^{-1}\)). The BPSK and QPSK data symbols have unit energy (\(\sigma_s^2 = 1\)), so the receiver uses \(\hat{\sigma}_n^2\) from section 4.1, clamped to \([0, 10]\). In a noiseless channel MMSE therefore reduces to ZF.

Common phase tracking. The channel estimate comes from the preamble only. A residual CFO error \(\epsilon\) rotates data symbol \(m\) by about \(2\pi \epsilon (m + 2) L / f_s\), and with about 10 active bins the CFO estimate is not precise enough to hold the phase over a long frame. Before equalization each data symbol is therefore derotated by the angle of its pilots against the channel estimate:

\[\theta_m = \angle \sum_{p} Y_m[k_p] \left(\hat{H}[k_p] X_p\right)^*\]

docs.title: 5. Channel Coding & Error Control
docs.text: Acoustic environments are prone to burst noise (e.g. key clicks, claps). We apply Forward Error Correction (FEC) to guarantee error-free recovery.

docs.title: 5.1 Reed-Solomon Code
docs.text:
A Reed-Solomon code \(RS(n, k)\) over the Galois Field \(GF(2^m)\) converts \(k\) data symbols into an \(n\)-symbol codeword.

  • Block Length: \(n = 2^m - 1\) symbols.
  • Message Size: \(k\) symbols.
  • Parity Bytes: \(2t = n - k\) symbols.
  • Error Correction Capability: The code can correct up to \(t\) symbol errors: $\(t = \lfloor \frac{n - k}{2} \rfloor\)$

The generator polynomial \(g(x)\) for the code is given by:

\[g(x) = \prod_{i=0}^{2t-1} \left( x - \alpha^{i + i_0} \right)\]

where \(\alpha\) is a primitive element of \(GF(2^m)\) and \(i_0\) is an integer offset (typically \(i_0 = 1\)).

docs.title: 5.2 Error Detection (CRC-32)
docs.text:
Before encoding with RS, the payload is appended with a Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC-32) checksum to verify frame integrity post-decoding. The CRC-32 generator polynomial is:

\[G(x) = x^{32} + x^{26} + x^{23} + x^{22} + x^{16} + x^{12} + x^{11} + x^{10} + x^8 + x^7 + x^5 + x^4 + x^2 + x + 1\]

docs.title: 6. Automatic Gain Control (AGC)
docs.text: Microphone sensitivity, speaker volume and distance change the received level by tens of dB. The RX pipeline normalizes the level before frame detection (native/src/agc/agc.c, issue #92). For each input sample \(x[n]\):

docs.title: 6.1 Power Estimate
docs.text:
A one-pole average of \(x^2\) approximates a 10 ms RMS window:

\[p[n] = p[n-1] + \alpha_{rms}\left(x[n]^2 - p[n-1]\right)\]

docs.title: 6.2 Desired and Smoothed Gain
docs.text:
\[g_d[n] = \operatorname{clamp}\!\left(\frac{A_{target}}{\sqrt{p[n] + \epsilon}},\; g_{min},\; g_{max}\right)\] \[g[n] = g[n-1] + \alpha\left(g_d[n] - g[n-1]\right), \qquad \alpha = \begin{cases} \alpha_{att} & g_d[n] < g[n-1] \text{ (attack)} \\ \alpha_{rel} & \text{otherwise (release)} \end{cases}\]

Each one-pole coefficient follows from its time constant \(\tau\):

\[\alpha_k = 1 - e^{-1/(\tau_k f_s)}\]

docs.title: 6.3 Peak Guard and Output
docs.text:
A frame arriving after silence would otherwise be multiplied by the silence gain for the first milliseconds. The gain is therefore capped instantly on peaks:

\[g[n] \leftarrow \min\!\left(g[n],\; \frac{L_{peak}}{|x[n]|}\right), \qquad y[n] = g[n]\, x[n], \quad |y[n]| \le L_{peak}\]

Non-finite samples produce \(y[n] = 0\) and leave \(p\) and \(g\) unchanged.

docs.title: 6.4 Parameters
docs.text:
Symbol Value Meaning \(A_{target}\) 0.25 (−12 dBFS) Output RMS target \(\tau_{rms}\) 10 ms Power-estimate window \(\tau_{att}\) / \(\tau_{rel}\) 1 ms / 100 ms Gain attack / release \([g_{min}, g_{max}]\) [0.1, 40] = [−20, +32] dB Gain range \(L_{peak}\) 1.0 Output peak limit (full scale)

The reported gain is \(G_{dB} = 20\log_{10} g\). Measured (test_agc): chirps 30 dB below to 10 dB above target settle within ±0.11 dB; convergence takes 10 ms after silence; cost is about 0.01 ms per 10 ms chunk.

Project: Soundwave — Ultrasonic Physical Layer Version: 1.0 Date: July 18, 2026 Author: PxA Labs (Archit Mittal, Purvansh Joshi)

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: Soundwave is a cross-platform application that enables short-range, device-to-device digital communication using ultrasonic audio waves (18–22 kHz). It maps digital bitstreams into high-frequency acoustic signals via consumer speakers and decodes them on the receiving side using microphones. The product targets Android (APK) and desktop platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux).

docs.title: 2. Problem Statement
docs.text: Current short-range wireless communication (Bluetooth, NFC) requires pairing, has protocol overhead, and is subject to frequency congestion. Ultrasonic communication offers a zero-infrastructure, pairing-free alternative for proximity-based data exchange using existing hardware (speakers and microphones) that every device already has.

docs.title: 3. Target Users
docs.text: Segment Use Case Developers & Researchers Experiment with acoustic PHY protocols, test chirp/OFDM modulation Security-Conscious Users Pairing-free, line-of-sight data exchange that is inherently hard to intercept remotely IoT Integrators Device discovery and bootstrap in environments where RF is restricted General Consumers Share small payloads (URLs, contacts, text) between nearby devices

docs.title: Dart API (Flutter app)
docs.text:
The complete, generated reference for every public library in soundwave_app/lib/ is the dart doc output. It is built by dart doc in the docs workflow, so it always matches the commit the site was built from.

soundwave_app is an application (publish_to: none), not a published package, so these APIs are internal and may change without notice. This page is a map of the most important types.

docs.title: Native bindings (lib/native/)
docs.text:
Type Purpose SoundwaveNative Singleton (SoundwaveNative.instance) that loads libsoundwave and wraps each sw_* function. On Android it loads libsoundwave.so. Desktop builds look next to the executable first (soundwave.dll, ../Frameworks/libsoundwave.dylib, lib/libsoundwave.so), then development build folders. $SOUNDWAVE_LIB overrides the path. Errors are thrown as SwException(code) SwConfig dart:ffi Struct mirroring sw_config_t field for field. A helper converts the app's config map into a native struct

Wrapper methods take and return Dart types such as Uint8List and Float32List. Buffers are sized with the C API's overflow protocol: try an estimate, and retry once with the size reported on SW_ERR_OVERFLOW.

docs.title: Engines (lib/engine/)
docs.text: Type Purpose FrameCodec App frame format [CRC-32][payload ≤ 219 B][RS parity 32 B]. encode builds a frame. decode searches candidate lengths until RS + CRC verify FrameGeometry Samples per symbol and preamble, and bits per symbol, for a config. Mirrors the native modulators and sizes the RX buffers TxEngine Encodes text or files, modulates on a background isolate and queues audio. Uses the link layer for long messages, files and ARQ RxEngine Capture loop: AGC → detectFrame → demodulate → FrameCodec.decode, then hands link frames to LinkReceiver. Exposes messages, transfers, constellation and frame-event streams link_frame.dart DATA / ACK / NACK frame encoding (magic byte 0xFA) and the message envelope (text or file, CRC-32, 1 MiB limit) PayloadFragmenter, PayloadReassembler Split envelopes into fragments of at most 208 B, and reassemble out-of-order fragments with duplicate suppression and idle timeouts ArqSender, ArqConfig Stop-and-wait ARQ with exponential backoff, jitter and NACK-triggered retransmission AgcProcessor Thin wrapper over the native AGC handle SignalMetrics, ThroughputCalculator, TxQueue Status bar metrics, throughput, and the transmit queue

docs.title: Frame formats
docs.text:
The app and soundwave-cli share one byte-level PHY frame, specified in the developer guide:

Producer Layout Length field App (engine/frame_codec.dart) and soundwave-cli (tools/soundwave_cli/frame_format.c) [CRC-32 LE over payload][payload 1..219 B][RS parity 32 B] None. The receiver takes the shortest length whose RS decode and CRC-32 verify

A WAV made by soundwave-cli modulate decodes in the app's Import Signal, and an app recording decodes with soundwave-cli demodulate (with the same modem settings). CI checks both directions (soundwave_app/test/native/cli_compat_test.dart).

The link layer (DATA/ACK/NACK frames, message envelope, reassembly and ARQ timing) runs inside the app frame's payload. It is specified in the developer guide.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text:
• Modulation and demodulation run on background isolates (compute) so the UI thread stays responsive. Imported files are decoded by OfflineDecoder.decodeInBackground.
  • Native audio callbacks run on miniaudio's device thread and exchange samples with Dart through ring buffers (sw_audio_capture_read / sw_audio_playback_write).
  • If the native audio service cannot be initialized, the app falls back to RecordAudioService (the record and audioplayers plugins, 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono).

docs.title: Signal chain & parameters
docs.text:
This page lists what the modulators actually generate on the current code, and the band, rate and airtime numbers that follow from it.

How to read the numbers

  • Derived values are computed from the formulas in native/src/css/css_modulate.c, native/src/ofdm/ofdm_modulate.c and soundwave_app/lib/engine/frame_geometry.dart. They are exact for the code, but they are not measurements.
  • Simulated values come from CI tests that add white Gaussian noise in software.
  • Measured over the air: none yet. See the field test plan.
  • Targets come from the PRD and are goals, not results.

docs.title: CSS (chirp) mode
docs.text:
Implementation (derived from code). sw_css_modulate sends LoRa-style chirp symbols: each data symbol is the base up-chirp cyclically shifted by \(k\) chips, \(k < M = 2^{SF}\), so one chirp carries SF bits (Gray mapped, MSB first). The band is carrier_freq ± \(B/2\), where \(B = f_s / D\) and \(D = \operatorname{round}(f_s / \text{bandwidth})\) samples per chip. A symbol lasts \(T = M/B\) (\(N = MD\) samples). Every frame starts with 8 base up-chirps and 2 down-chirps; data are up-chirps only. symbol_duration is not used by CSS. Formulas, the receiver and the reasons for the SF range are in Mathematical model §2.1.
